## Request

Assess source readiness for **Mattress Firm Holding Corp.**, as of **2014-09-11**, for the requested credit snapshot: the financial-data foundation (CP-1) and legal/covenant analysis (CP-4). This is a source-sufficiency review, not a credit conclusion, legal interpretation, investment recommendation, or certification of downstream analytical completion.

The dated context is a user input, not issuer evidence. Its blank current/prior-period and cutoff fields remain unspecified. Historical coverage is identified from filing contents rather than filenames. Proposed financing inputs must remain separate from reported outstanding facilities.

### Readiness view

The source set supports historical financial-data work with bounded limitations. It does not support a complete interpretation of the existing or proposed financing package without the governing financing documents. Acquisition announcements and an executed asset purchase agreement provide useful transaction evidence, but target financials, omitted schedules, and closing evidence remain incomplete. Extraction has been inspected selectively; the full source set has not been fidelity-certified.

### Located financial coverage and reporting basis

**Annual authority and perimeter.** K page 1 states “For the fiscal year ended January 28, 2014” and identifies “MATTRESS FIRM HOLDING CORP.” K page 5 defines the group as “Mattress Firm Holding Corp. and its consolidated subsidiaries” and says the year is described as “fiscal 2013.” K pages 89–90 contain the auditor's report, including “present fairly, in all material respects” and “in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.” K page 92 separately contains the predecessor auditor's report for earlier comparative years. These support an audited historical consolidated foundation, not audited standalone borrower accounts.

K pages 92–95 locate balance sheets, operations, stockholders' equity, and cash flows; statement headers specify “in thousands” with share/per-share exceptions. K pages 95–96 establish the business and consolidation basis. K page 54 describes a retail reportable segment and states: “Franchise operations are a separate reportable segment,” with results represented by franchise fees and royalty income on the statements. Thus segment coverage is available at the disclosed level; regional operating segments must not be mistaken for separately supplied regional financial statements.

**Interim periods and units.** QA pages 3–6 locate balance sheets, discrete-quarter operations and cash flows, and basis notes. QJ pages 3–7 locate balance sheets, discrete-quarter and YTD operations, YTD cash flows, and basis notes. The QJ contents explicitly distinguish “thirteen weeks” from “twenty-six weeks”; its cash-flow statement is YTD, not a discrete-quarter statement. QJ page 5 includes “Cash paid for:” with interest and income taxes. Financial statement headers use “In thousands” with stated share/per-share exceptions. Reporting currency is USD in user settings; issuer statement dollar signs support dollar-denominated reporting, but a separate explicit currency-code legend was not located. No unit conversion has been performed.

QA page 5 and QJ page 5 say the interim accounts are “unaudited” and that financial information and footnotes “have been condensed or omitted”; both direct the reader to the annual statements. These omissions are bounded by retaining the annual report rather than treating either interim as a self-contained full annual disclosure package.

**Comparability and measurement cautions.** QA page 6 and QJ pages 6–7 disclose the inventory accounting change and cash-flow reclassifications. QJ page 6 says the change “has not been retrospectively applied to prior periods”; page 7 says cash-flow reclassification had “no effect” on previously reported operating cash flow. These are source basis differences to carry into extraction, not authorization to restate figures. The fiscal-calendar basis differs across FY2013 and FY2014; the source says: “The fiscal year ended January 28, 2014 (‘Fiscal 2013’) consisted of 52 weeks” and “Fiscal 2014” “consists of 53 weeks” [QJ page 7]. Period labels therefore control; calendar-year assumptions do not.

**Adjusted figures, KPIs, and narrative.** K pages 50–51, QA pages 29–31, and QJ pages 37–39 locate non-GAAP definitions, GAAP bridges, add-back categories, and footnotes. K page 50 and QJ page 38 explicitly warn that future expenses may be “the same as or similar to” adjustments presented. QJ page 39 identifies acquisition accounting and cash integration costs together in the acquisition-related adjustment and describes ERP costs within other adjustments. The bridge supports reported-data extraction, not a determination that all add-backs are recurring, nonrecurring, acceptable, or achievable.

QJ pages 22–23 provide quarter/YTD management discussion, comparable-store sales, and a progression in sales split between comparable, new, acquired, and closed stores. K page 54 supplies annual business and segment narrative. QJ page 37 provides seasonality and a management compliance assertion. These are usable located supporting disclosures; CP-1 must preserve management attribution and not convert a covenant-compliance assertion into a verified headroom calculation.

### Acquisition coverage and evidence hierarchy

E page 1 reports entry into the Back to Bed agreement; page 2 states closing “remains subject to customary closing conditions” and that the company “expects to fund the purchase price from cash on hand and revolver borrowings.” A page 1 is marked “Execution Version”; page 57 states “the Parties hereto have executed this Agreement” and includes the buyer's textual signature. This establishes a filed executed agreement, not consummation of the acquisition.

A pages 10–14 locate purchase-price and working-capital definitions, vendor-payment and lease adjustments, cash/escrow payment mechanics, and closing conditions. For example, section 2.1 states: “The aggregate purchase price ... shall be $60,000,000, subject to certain adjustments as set forth herein” [A page 10]. Section 2.2 refers to historical accounting practices in a schedule [A page 10]. A pages 57–58 explicitly identify omitted schedules, including financial statements, net sales by facility, encumbrances, leases, and undisclosed liabilities. The operative text is retained, but its cross-references are not complete evidence of the underlying assets or liabilities.

A page 58 labels the attachment “Form of Escrow Agreement” and begins “as of August [ ], 2014.” That form is not evidence of an executed escrow agreement or a funded escrow account. P page 1 provides attributed strategic rationale, while P page 2 labels benefit statements forward-looking. Its overlap with E and A is corroboration, not a basis to prefer management language over operative text. No material conflict was identified in the inspected acquisition description; this is not a conflict clearance for uninspected clauses.

QJ pages 20–21 disclose Best Mattress, Back to Bed, and The Sleep Train transactions as subsequent events relative to the reporting period. The Sleep Train disclosure says the company “entered into an agreement to acquire all of the outstanding equity interests in The Sleep Train, Inc.” and “anticipates this transaction will close in the fourth quarter of 2014” [QJ page 21]. QJ page 43 search-located signatures are dated “September 5, 2014.” Thus the disclosed agreement predates the run date, while anticipated closing remains forward-looking. These transactions must not be included as already-owned operations merely because they appear in the latest interim report. Standalone target financials, the Sleep Train agreement, and final financing evidence are not supplied.

### Preparation, extraction fidelity, and coverage disposition

Only supplied text was available. Located content establishes documentary family and authority, but successful text retrieval is not visual validation or full parsing certification. No images, charts, original signatures, hyperlinks, speaker notes, hidden workbook content, formulas, or caches were visually inspected. No workbook or deck is supplied. No complete earnings release or guidance package is supplied; P is an acquisition announcement.

A specific text defect is retained rather than silently repaired: QJ page 13 reads “at the Company's operation” and gives an incomplete alternative rate clause, “or (ii) the period relevant to such borrowing adjusted for certain additional costs.” QA page 12 contains a fuller LIBOR description. The earlier passage helps identify the defect but cannot establish the later governing legal wording. Source risk is unreliable extraction or source wording in that clause; downstream consequence is that exact interest-definition use requires original-text verification and governing documents.

## Calculations

No arithmetic, normalization, reconciliation, conversion, derived period, ratio, or fabricated financial figure was produced. The source-readiness method prohibits those activities at this stage. All monetary figures and calendar-length quantities appearing above are exact source quotations; source page locators and identifiers are not calculations. Missing quantities remain **Not supplied**; any proposed transaction aggregate or covenant headroom is **Not calculable** here because the required governing and target evidence is incomplete and calculation is outside this review.

The strongest contrary evidence to broad readiness is the missing governing financing documentation and the agreement's explicit schedule omissions. Conversely, these gaps do not render the located audited and unaudited historical statements unusable. Readiness is therefore split by consumer rather than globally approved or blocked.
